---
title: "Research pipeline"
---

The research code lives in **`pipeline/` in this repository**. It prepares the observations, builds the features, evaluates the five components and refits the production models. The inference package, `PRESS/`, loads exported models and does not run this training code.

The pipeline represents **one complete run**. Its inputs and outputs are explicit; it does not search previous experiments for interrupted fits or partially completed jobs.

## Code layout

```text
pipeline/
  run.py                       # complete dependency-ordered run
  folds.json                   # fixed match partitions
  preprocessing/
    01_tracking.py             # raw observations and tracking derivatives
    02_possessions.py          # matched control intervals and segmentation
    03_bases.py                # broad action and drive observations
    04_context_inputs.py       # event tables for fold-specific xT
    library.py
  <task>/                      # ball_drive, pass_probability, pass_selection,
                               # action_selection, residual_risk
    01_features.py
    02_train.py
    03_scores.py
    04_refit.py
    filters.py                 # task-specific selection rules
    library.py                 # task orchestration
    protocol.json              # fixed settings and search grids
  composed_risk/
    01_compute.py              # held-out h and xLoss
    02_scores.py               # metrics, calibration and band bootstrap
  library/
    common.py                  # paths, encoding, checksums and metrics
    states.py                  # initial states and known-at-frame context
    expected_threat.py         # fitting-only smoothing selection and 10 × 6 xT
    option_features.py         # physical and hypothetical pass fields
    binary_training.py         # native binary XGBoost training
    ball_drive/                # spline bases, MAP likelihood and export
    pass_probability/          # flight boundaries, trajectory MLE and transfer
    pass_selection/            # grouped choice likelihood and utility fitting
    preprocessing/             # source adapters and segmentation helpers
```

Each task has the same four entry points. Shared functions live in `library/`; the `filters.py` beside a task states its own eligibility rules. The raw-data adapter is specific to the SkillCorner release. The [package input interfaces](api.qmd) also accept canonical tables from other tracking providers.

## Four stages per task

| Stage | Purpose | Saved outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `01_features.py` | Apply the task's cohort rules and calculate features from the current run's inputs. | Stable observation keys, feature tables or matrices, physical arrays, feature specifications. |
| `02_train.py` | Fit and select models using the declared match splits. | Fold models, validation choices, learning curves or optimization diagnostics, posterior quantities where applicable, held-out predictions. |
| `03_scores.py` | Combine the held-out predictions and calculate final scores. | Pooled predictions, metrics and calibration bins. Pass selection reports both flat and cross-nested families. |
| `04_refit.py` | Fit operational models on the full development sample using the selected procedure. | Exported JSON manifests, adjacent UBJ ensembles, or the physical model's parameters and posterior. |

The [general benchmark protocol](benchmark.qmd) explains the distinction between validation, held-out evaluation and production refitting. The individual benchmark pages document the task-specific targets and selection procedures: [ball drive](benchmarks/01_ball_drive_risk.qmd), [pass probability](benchmarks/02_pass_probability.qmd), [pass selection](benchmarks/03_pass_selection.qmd), [action selection](benchmarks/04_action_selection.qmd), [residual risk](benchmarks/05_residual_risk.qmd) and [composed risk](benchmarks/06_composed_risk.qmd).

## Dependency order

1. Prepare tracking, matched individual possessions and canonical checkpoints. Preserve the broad observations; outcome-based task filters are applied later.
2. Fit **ball-drive risk** and **pass probability**. These two components can be run independently.
3. Calculate **pass-selection** features using the physical models fitted on the six training matches of the corresponding fold and fit-match-only xT. Fit both choice families; the flat family supplies the downstream models.
4. Calculate **action-selection** features using the matching physical and pass-selection models, calibrated pass success and BCOS. Fit the native binary classifier.
5. Calculate **residual-risk** features from the same state summaries, observed elapsed time and P(carry). Training P(carry) is cross-fitted inside the six fit matches; validation and test use the corresponding action-selection model.
6. Compose held-out **h and xLoss**, then calculate their scores and the fixed-threshold match bootstrap.
7. Refit the production stack in the same dependency order. Full-data features are generated separately with `01_features.py --production-features` for the three tree-model tasks. Production residual-risk features use five eight-fit/two-held action models for P(carry).

A production model never substitutes for a fold-specific model in the benchmark feature stack. The final refits are exports for inference, not additional held-out evaluations.

### Following the xT calculation

The xT implementation is in [expected_threat.py](pipeline/library/expected_threat.py). Its reading order is:

1. `prepare`: build the four event tables using the archived extraction rules.
2. `rebin`, `transition`, `goal_probability`, `xt_model`: assign cells, estimate destination distributions and goal probability, then solve the Bellman equation. Event frequencies are not smoothed.
3. `component_scores`, `select_bandwidth`: evaluate the candidate Gaussian bandwidths by leave-one-match-out on the fitting matches. Select the largest bandwidth within one paired-match standard error of the best score.
4. `fit_on_matches`: apply that selection separately to passes, carries and goal given shot, then fit the surface on all requested fitting matches. Its result includes the surface, component arrays, chosen bandwidths and validation tables.
5. `fit`: load the event tables and return the surface to the downstream feature builder.

The same procedure uses the six fitting matches for each feature fold and all ten matches for production. The production bandwidths (8, 5 and 5 m) are results of selection, not constants imposed on every fold. In the accepted six-match fits, the goal bandwidth is 8 m in folds 0 and 4 and 5 m in the remaining folds; the pass and carry bandwidths are 8 and 5 m throughout. The [xT vignette](vignettes/extras/expected_threat/11.expected_threat.ipynb) distinguishes the event frequencies from the transition matrices and explains both uses of Gaussian smoothing.

## Run the pipeline

From the repository checkout, install the package and parquet support in the documented Python environment:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[io]'
```

The [runner](pipeline/run.py) first prints the complete command sequence. Supply a **new output directory**:

```bash
python -m pipeline.run \
  --raw-root /path/to/opendata/data/matches \
  --output-root /path/to/research_outputs/press_final \
  --threads 8
```

Add `--execute` to execute that sequence. The runner stops at the first failed command and does not submit cluster jobs or install new weights into `PRESS/utils/data`.

The numbered scripts can also be launched separately. For example:

```bash
python pipeline/ball_drive/01_features.py \
  --base-root /path/to/research_outputs/press_final/base \
  --output-root /path/to/research_outputs/press_final

python pipeline/ball_drive/02_train.py \
  --base-root /path/to/research_outputs/press_final/base \
  --output-root /path/to/research_outputs/press_final \
  --fold 0
```

`--fold` selects a fitting fold; omitting it runs all five. Feature calculation can be partitioned with repeatable `--match` arguments. The fold partitions and the fit-only vocabularies remain fixed when feature jobs are split across workers. Run a scores stage only after every required fold has finished. `JAX_ENABLE_X64=1` is required for fitting the physical models; the complete runner sets it explicitly.

## Output layout

```text
research_outputs/press_final/
  base/
    matches/<match_id>/         # observations, identities, intervals and actions
    xt/                        # event tables; xT itself is fitted per split
    manifest.json
    coverage.csv
  ball_drive/
    features/<match_id>/
    training/fold_<n>/
    scores/
    production/
  pass_probability/
  pass_selection/
  action_selection/
  residual_risk/
  composed_risk/
    features/
    scores/
```

Every task has dedicated folders. JSON files record settings, feature order, learned category levels and model dependencies; numerical arrays use NPZ/NPY or Parquet, and tree ensembles use UBJ. Stage manifests record completed outputs and their checksums. Existing nonempty outputs are protected against accidental replacement.

## Verification

Feature construction was checked against the accepted cohorts: **9,114 ball-drive observations, 6,706 pass-probability observations, 6,810 pass-selection choices, 16,918 action-selection decisions and 7,820 residual-risk observations**. A raw-to-base reconstruction was checked on an observed match, and the reconstructed production xT surface matches the saved surface. Numerical checks compare the extracted physical likelihood with the public evaluator. The distributed model files are checksum-protected and are not refitted by these checks.

A full research rerun is an explicit, computationally expensive operation and is not part of these checks, which do not constitute a new benchmark.
